en: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Heart of Amoghapāśa"
Oṃ. Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Heart of the Unfailing Lasso.
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling on Mount Potalaka,
in the abode of the noble Avalokiteśvara, which was adorned with many *śāla*, *tamāla*, *campaka*, *aśoka*, and *atimuktaka* trees and various other kinds of trees,
together with a great community of monks, eighteen thousand in number.

Surrounded and honored by nine hundred and ninety thousand nayutas of kotis of bodhisattvas, and by many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of sons of the gods from the Śuddhāvāsa heaven, he taught the Dharma with reference to the sons of the gods belonging to the classes of Īśvara, Maheśvara, and Brahmakāyika.

Then indeed, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and, extending his joined palms toward the Blessed One and bowing down, with a smiling countenance, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

“Blessed One, I possess a heart-mantra named Amoghapāśarāja, which I previously received from the presence of the Tathāgata named Lokendrarāja in the world-system called Vilokitā during the ninety-first eon.

By means of this, Blessed One, many hundreds of thousands of devaputras—headed by the devaputras Īśvara, Devamaheśvara, and Mahādeva, as well as the Śuddhāvāsakāyika devaputras—were inspired toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; and I myself attained hundreds of thousands of samādhis, headed by the Samādhi of the Array of Non-delusive Knowledge.”
Furthermore, Blessed One, in whatever place on earth this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* shall circulate,

it should be known, Blessed One, that in that place on earth twelve hundred thousand sons of gods, headed by Īśvara, Maheśvara, and the Brahmakāyikas, will remain for the sake of protection, defense, and guardianship; and that place on earth, Blessed One, will be regarded as a *caitya*.

Blessed One, those beings who hear this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* of mine will have planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas; wherever this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* shall circulate.
Whosoever, O Blessed One, might be a committer of sins, a locus for all evils, one who practices unwholesome dharmas, a reviler of the noble ones, a rejecter of the true Dharma,
one destined for the Avīci hell, and a rejecter of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, noble Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas;
If it should spread further,
one incurs a transgression of the vow.
Blessed One, for one who performs even a single recitation of the *upavāha*, that karma is purified right here in this very life.
It goes to total exhaustion and is vomited out;
by means of a fever that occurs every day, every two days, every three days, or every four days, or likewise by a fever that occurs every seven days;
or by pain in the eyes, pain in the ears, or pain in the nose.
Or with pain in the teeth and lips, or pain in the tongue,
or pain in the palate, or pain in the heart, or pain in the abdomen, or pain in the sides, or pain in the hips,
or pain in the limbs and minor members, or pain from hemorrhoids and dysentery, or by diarrhea, or by affliction of the hands and feet, or by headache— [may there be] a variegated rain-cloud.

Whether by leprosy, boils, scabies, ringworm, skin diseases, hemorrhoids, fistulas, bites, eruptions, epilepsy, or what is known as *kākhorda* (sorcery), or by curses, misdeeds, imprisonment, binding, beating, threats, or the afflictions of malevolent spirits;
in short, O Blessed One, whether through physical pain, mental anguish, or the sight of bad dreams, that karma reaches its exhaustion.
It becomes completely purified;

how much more so for pure beings who are resolved through faith! Blessed One, if the four assemblies and the four castes, even those who are deceitful or fraudulent, should hear this Amoghapāśahṛdaya.

They will take it up, uphold it, recite it, write it down, cause it to be written down, master it, and cause other beings— even those among the animal realm— to hear it, or, standing at the side of their ear, provide them with whispered instruction.
And they will contemplate these mantra-words:
as non-rejection, as non-arising,
as non-departure, as non-action, as freedom from afflictions, as casting forth equal reflection, and as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the five aggregates.
By this yoga, the recollection of the Buddhas (buddhānusmṛti) should be performed;
they will cause a thousand Buddhas from the ten directions to appear before one's eyes,
and they will perform the confession of transgressions.
...and so on, up to: or having had it written in a book, they will keep it in their homes.
What need is there to say more, Blessed One? They will listen even out of mutual faith.

Whether out of fear of their masters, or due to others' commands, or for the sake of avoiding public censure, they will listen. O Blessed One, it should be understood that by the power of the noble Avalokiteśvara, a sound issues forth into the hollows of their ears, saying, "This must be known."

“Blessed One, it is just as if some man were to drag out sandalwood, camphor, or musk, and having reviled them, were to grind them on a stone and smear himself with them. Yet that sandalwood, camphor, or musk does not think: ‘I have been dragged out and reviled; I shall overwhelm [him] with my fragrance.’”
Moreover, O Blessed One, this very heart-mantra of mine named Amoghapāśa is like a fragrance; whoever, having taken it up or recited it—
even as far as honoring it with the sound of "māyā" or even with a mere substitute for provisions— [shall obtain the fruit].
Blessed One, for those beings of the air, that very root of merit will be their cause;
wherever they are reborn,
there they shall never be deprived of the fragrance of the equipment of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, and merit, and it makes them truly fragrant with ethical discipline.

Blessed One, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, monk or nun, layman or laywoman, or anyone else, having dedicated themselves to the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya, should observe the fast on the eighth day of the bright fortnight;
they should recite the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya seven times without speaking to anyone.
"Blessed One, in this very life, twenty benefits are to be expected for him.
What are the twenty?
Namely, that diseases will not arise in his body."
Furthermore, the diseases that have arisen in him will, through the power of his karma, quickly subside;
he will possess limbs that are supple, beautiful, and smooth,
and he will become beloved by many people.
Their sense faculties will be guarded, and they will obtain wealth;
they will acquire wealth as it arises,
and it shall not be consumed by fire nor swept away by water.
The king will not be able to remove evil with his mind;
his undertakings will flourish,
and there will be no fear of lightning or water.
There will be no fear of wind or rain.
Having consecrated either ashes or water seven times with the Amoghapāśahṛdaya, one should perform the binding of the field in all directions, intermediate directions, above, and below;
all calamities will be pacified.
Those who steal vitality will not be able to take away his vitality;
he will become dear to all sentient beings and will be pleasing to their minds.
He shall have no fear of enemies;
and whatever fear of enemies has arisen for him shall quickly be pacified.
Furthermore, he shall have no fear of human beings.
There shall be no fear of *kākhorda* spells for him, nor fear of *ḍākinīs*, nor shall he experience intense afflictions or secondary afflictions.
He shall not meet his end by fire, by weapon, or by poison.
And deities shall constantly and perpetually stand ready to provide him with protection, shelter, and defense.
Wherever they may be reborn, in each of those places they will never be separated from loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
These twenty benefits are to be expected;
furthermore, they will attain eight other qualities.
What are the eight?
At the time of death, the noble Avalokiteśvara will grant a face-to-face vision in the form of a monk. (1)
He will pass away with ease. // 2 //
One will not have a deluded vision. // 3 //
He will not make a gesture with his hand. // 4 //
He will not take a step. // 5 //
He will not die while defecating, nor while urinating, nor while mounted on a vehicle.
His mindfulness will be well-established in happiness. // 7 //
He shall not die with his face turned downward. // 8 //
At the time of death, he will possess inexhaustible eloquence;
he will be reborn in whichever Buddha-field he has made a vow for;
and he will never be separated from virtuous friends.
It should be recited three times each day, at the three periods of the day.
One must avoid liquor, meat, onions, garlic, and food left over from others; one who seeks the prosperity of the realm should abstain from these.
Furthermore, this Dharma discourse called the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* should be made heard after having ascertained the strength and weakness of all sentient beings.
One must not practice the "teacher's fist" (withholding knowledge).
For Bodhisattvas are those who have departed from the stains of envy and possessiveness, and who act for the benefit of sentient beings.
Through acting for the benefit of sentient beings, the awakening of a Buddha is attained; thus, "awakening" refers to wisdom (*prajñā*), and "being" (*sattva*) refers to skillful means (*upāya*).
"These two dharmas are not found for the sake of sentient beings.

If the Blessed One would grant me permission, I shall proclaim this heart-mantra before the Tathāgata for the benefit of the fourfold assembly. Having said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, he spoke as follows.
"Speak this, O Pure Being, at whatever time you deem appropriate.
It has been approved by the Tathāgata that in the future time, in the final age, they shall perform the work of a father for those who belong to the Bodhisattva vehicle.
Then, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, with eyes free from blinking, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

Listen to me, Blessed One: this maṇḍala of the gateways to liberation, which is honored by all bodhisattvas, is for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, and for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings.

Homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas established throughout the three times; homage to the assemblies of Pratyekabuddhas and noble Śrāvakas of the past, future, and present; homage to those who have gone rightly;
homage to those who have practiced rightly;
homage to Śāradvatīputra, the great lord of generosity.

Homage to the assembly of great bodhisattvas headed by the noble Maitreya. Homage to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present. Homage to the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇaprabha. Homage to the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vipaśyin. Homage to the Tathāgata Śikhin, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Homage to the Tathāgata Viśvabhū.
Homage to the Tathāgata Krakucchanda.
Homage to the Tathāgata Kanakamuni. Homage to the Tathāgata Kāśyapa.
Homage to Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. It is as follows:
Oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā / Oṃ same same mahāsame rakṣa rakṣa māṃ and all sentient beings from all evils, O pacifier of all evils, svāhā.
Homage to the Tathāgata Suparikīrtitanāmadheya. Homage to the Tathāgata Samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāmaśrī. Homage to the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Tathāgata Indraketudhvajaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha Vikrāntagāmin.
Homage to the Buddha; homage to the Dharma; homage to the Saṅgha.
Homage to the Blessed Buddhas of the past, future, and present. It is as follows:
O increaser of mindfulness, increaser of conduct, increaser of steadfastness, increaser of wisdom, increaser of eloquence, increaser of meditative concentration, increaser of power,
increaser of all factors conducive to enlightenment, you who bring to fulfillment all the qualities of a Buddha, svāhā!
Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One!

Having paid homage to these, I shall now recite this Heart Sūtra named the Amoghapāśarāja, which was uttered by the Tathāgata from the mouth of the noble Avalokiteśvara in the midst of a great assembly. May my mantra-words and all my undertakings be successful!
May there be protection for me and for all sentient beings from all fears. It is as follows:
Oṃ cara cara ciri ciri curū curū mara mara miri miri murū murū Mahākāruṇika!
Sara sara siri siri surū surū curū curū ciri ciri viri viri piri piri miri miri Mahāpadāhasta!
Kala kala kili kili kulu kulu Mahāśuddhasattva!
Buddhaya 2, bodha 2, bodhi 2, bodhaya 2, kaṇa 2, kiṇi 2, kuṇu 2, O Paramaśuddhasattva!
Kara 2, kiri 2, kurū 2, O Mahāsthāmaprāpta!
Move, move! Move together, move together! Move apart, move apart! Eṭaṭa, eṭaṭa! Bhara, bhara! Bhiri, bhiri! Bhurū, bhurū! Tara, tara! Tiri, tiri! Turū, turū! Come, O Great Compassionate One!
You who wear the guise of Mahāpaśupati!
Dhara 2, dhiri 2, dharū 2; tara 2, sara 2, cara 2; para 2, vara 2, mara 2; lara 2, hara 2; hāhā, hīhī, hūhū!
Oṃ! O Brahmā, Lord of the Earth, uphold!

Uphold! Dhiri! Dhiri! Dhurū! Dhurū! Cross over! Cross over! Move! Move! Pass beyond! Be supreme! Hara! Hara! You whose body is adorned with a thousand rays; blaze! Blaze! Heat! Heat! Shine! Shine! Wander! Wander! O Blessed One, honored at your feet by the moon, the sun, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Brahmā, Indra, Vāyu, Agni, Dhanada, and the hosts of ṛṣis and gods!
*Surū surū curū curū murū murū dhurū dhurū! Sanatkumāra, Rudra, Vāsava, Viṣṇu, Dhanada, Vāyu, Agni, Ṛṣi, Nāyaka, Vināyaka!
Wearer of many various guises!

*Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhurū dhurū tara tara thara thara dhara dhara para para lara lara hara hara yara yara sara sara vara vara, O Giver of Boons! Samantāvalokita, Lokeśvara, Lord of the Three Worlds, Possessor of All Virtues!*
O well-adorned Avalokiteśvara!

*muhu* 2, *murū* 2, *muya* 2, *muṃca* 2, protect me and all sentient beings from all fears, from all calamities, from all misfortunes, from all seizing spirits, from all diseases, from all poisons, and from all fevers!
Thus, [you are] the liberator from bondage, imprisonment, beating, threats, kings, thieves, fire, water, poison, and weapons;
*kaṇa 2 kiṇi 2 kuṇu 2 cara 2 ciri 2 curū 2*, the one who fully reveals the faculties, the powers, the factors of awakening, and the four noble truths.
Tama, dama, sama, masa, dhama, O Greatly Compassionate One, Dispeller of the Great Darkness of Ignorance, Fulfilled One of the Six Perfections!
mala 2 mili 2 mulu 2 / ṭa ṭa ṭa ṭa / ṭha ṭha ṭha ṭha /
ḍi ḍi ḍi ḍi / ṭu ṭu ṭu ṭu / ṭhi ṭhi ṭhi ṭhi /
Dhu dhu dhu dhu! O you who have a belt made of antelope skin! Come, come, O Great Compassionate One!
O Īśvara, Maheśvara, destroyer of the hosts of great beings! Kara 2 kiri 2 kurū 2 para 2 hara 2 hiri 2 vara 2 sara 2 kara 2 kaṭa 2 kiṭi 2 kuṭu 2 maṭa 2!
O Great Pure Being, dweller in the realm, Great Compassionate One, wearer of the white sacrificial thread, jewel-crowned, and bearer of garlands!

O you who have placed the most wonderful matted locks and crown upon the head of the Omniscient One; O you adorned with lotuses, whose palms possess the meditative concentration and liberation of dhyāna; O you who are unshakable and who surround the continuums of many beings; O Great Compassionate One, purifier of all karmic obscurations, fulfiller of the wisdom of the Omniscient One!
Homage to you who liberates from all diseases,
who fulfills all sentient beings,
and who bestows equal seats upon all sentient beings; svāhā!
Svāhā to Amogha! Svāhā to Amoghapāśa! Svāhā to Ajita!
Svāhā to Aparājitā!
Svāhā to Amitābha! Svāhā to the son of Amitābha!
Svāhā to the crusher of Māra’s army!
Svāhā to the bestower of fearlessness!
Svāhā to Yama!
To Vijaya, svāhā!
To Jaya and Vijaya, svāhā!
This is my ritual action; homage to you, svāhā!
oṃ raṇa raṇa oṃ phaṭ svāhā / oṃ jaya huṃ phaṭ svāhā / oṃ jupi svāhā /
Oṃ jaya svāhā / Oṃ hrīḥ trailokyavijayāmoghapāśapratihata hrīṃ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā / Oṃ vasumati svāhā /
Oṃ ārolīka svāhā / Oṃ bahule bahule svāhā / Oṃ ārolika hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā // //

In all fevers, a thread should be bound with mustard seeds, *vadira* wood pegs, and so forth; for all diseases, clarified butter, oil, or water should be given after consecrating it with recitation (*parijapya*).

For the destruction of sorcery (*kākhorda*), protection is provided by means of a thread; for abdominal pain, by means of a weapon; for poison, salt-water; and for eye disease, earth or water. For toothache, a *karavīra* tooth-stick should be used; a white thread should be tied to the ear.

In the rite of binding the boundary (*sīmābandha*), one should recite the five-colored thread twenty-one times, tie it to four stakes of *khadira* wood, and drive them into the ground in the four directions; thus the boundary is bound.
For all protections, one may use the thread, water, or ashes against all planetary seizures (*graha*).
For all fevers, use a five-colored thread; for seizures by snakes, insects, scorpions, *lohaliṅgala*, and the like, use a white thread.
In cases of eye disease, [one should use] honey combined with *pippalī*.
For all quarrels, strife, and disputes, one should rinse the mouth after consecrating water with the recitation [of the mantra], using either scented water, *palāśa* water, or honey-water.
In foreign lands, kingdoms, or territories, one should place a full jar [of water] there; then, by a pure person dressed in clean garments, having performed a great worship, it should be recited.
Great peace arises;
one should sprinkle with that water, whereby protection is established for all sentient beings,
and all calamities and misfortunes are pacified.

For one who has been consecrated, a sandalwood tilaka should be applied to the heart after reciting the mantra twenty-one times; all acts of immediate retribution (ānantarya) will be exhausted. By constant recitation, there is protection of the home;
by an oblation of lotuses, there is protection for all sentient beings.

Through the *candana-homa* (sandalwood oblation), there is protection against all *bhūtas*, *grahas*, and *rakṣas*. [The herbs are] *jaya*, *vijayā*, *aparājitā*, *nākulī*, *gandhanākūlī*, *dhāraṇī*, and *abhayapāṇi*.
Indriyapāṇi;
and the fragrances: priyaṅgu, tagara, cakrā, mahācakrā, viṣṇukrāntā, somarājī, and sūnandā—of these, as available.

Having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times and consecrated a jewel, it should be worn on the head or the arm. When worn around the neck by children or at the waist by women, it brings supreme good fortune;
O Jewel, it bestows the attainment of prosperity and grants sons.
By wearing this jewel, all protection is accomplished;
poison and fire do not overcome one,
and no harm caused by poison arises.
Even when they have arisen, they will not cause suffering;
they will be quickly pacified.
By means of water, this rite acts as a stambhana (paralyzer) for wind, clouds, and lightning, and performs all functions through its pervasive presence.
The Heart of Noble Avalokiteśvara is supremely effective; even if not formally consecrated, it performs these rites. Now, for one who wishes to practice its consecration, there are two methods.
On a cloth, having painted an image of the Buddha using pure pigments, one should depict Noble Avalokiteśvara wearing a crown of matted locks.

Having fashioned a belt from the skin of an eneya antelope and assuming the appearance of Paśupati, adorned with all ornaments, one should have the image painted by a painter who has observed the poṣadha vows.
Then, the practitioner, having made a mandala out of cow dung before it and scattering white flowers upon it, should place eight jars filled with scented water.
There are eight offerings and sixty-four requisites.
One should recite the mantra eight thousand times while offering a sacrifice of meat devoid of blood and burning agarwood incense,
having fasted for either a day and night or just the night.
Having eaten food that is pure of three kinds, having bathed at the three times of day, and having put on clean garments, one should perform the recitation.
Then, from the image, one sees oneself depicted [therein].
Seeing this, one rejoices until, in a dream, the Noble Avalokiteśvara appears.
He fulfills all [desires].
Having recited the mantra over realgar or silver and having applied it to his eyes, he then becomes invisible;
he traverses the sky.
He attains the samādhi called the Array of Non-delusion;
whatever he desires, that he accomplishes—such is the practitioner.
Thus spoke the Blessed One. The noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the monks in both their physical forms and their voices,
those Bodhisattvas, the sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas,
rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Heart of the Unfailing Lasso" is completed.
Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has explained their cause, as well as their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa.
